newsitem.title: USA: Kantor says U.S. exports heading for record in 96.
newsitem.headline: Kantor says U.S. exports heading for record in 96.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor said Thursday that U.S. exports would likely reach a record this year.

"Exports for the first ten months of this year are running six percent over their level of a year ago, and heading to a new record level once again this year," Kantor said in a telephone conference with reporters.

Kantor, who was on vacation in Hawaii, spoke to reporters after the Commerce Department reported that the U.S. trade deficit shrank by 30 percent to $7.99 billion in October from a revised $11.44 billion in September. It was the lowest monthly gap in seven months.
"The improvement in the October trade deficit is evidence that the economy is continuing to grow in a sustainable fashion in the fourth quarter," Kantor said.

The outgoing commerce secretary said a sharp rise in the monthly trade deficit with Japan reflected higher car imports due to the new model year. The U.S. deficit with Japan normally increases in September and October as dealers stock up on new cars, Kantor said.

The deficit with Japan rose by 30.9 percent to $4.96 billion in October, the highest level since $5 billion in August 1995. The deficit with Japan barely surpassed the $4.90 billion deficit with China.

Kantor blamed discrimination against U.S. products by China for the huge trade gap. He said the United States needed to continue to work on opening up what he called China's sanctuary markets to more U.S.-made goods.
